characters.role: your cheerful jungle guide and friend
a chatty little parrot who rides on your backpack

coverMeta.personalizedTitle: Alex and the Kindly Jungle Helpers
coverMeta.dedication: For Alex, the kindest explorer in the jungle

pages.text:
Green leaves wave hello as you and your guide Sam step into the warm, friendly jungle. A small parrot named Robin rides on your backpack, chirping about all the animals who might need a hand today.

"In this jungle, we help with small problems and share big smiles," says Sam. Just then you hear a sniffly sound up the trail.

choices.text: Peek toward a splashy river sound

pages.text:
You find a little monkey sitting on a branch, sniffling because the wind took its favorite red hat. Robin flutters up for a better look while Sam pats the monkey gently.

"We can help you find it," you say. The monkey points one way toward a tall tree and another way toward a bushy path.

By the river, a big friendly elephant is giggling and splashing, but every splash makes her sneeze. "My trunk is so ticklish today," she says, wobbling with giggles.

Sam grins. "A ticklish trunk is a very serious jungle problem." Robin nods wisely, or maybe just bobs for fun.

choices.text: Try a soft leaf to help the trunk

pages.text:
You climb toward the tall tree with Sam steadying the branches. Up in the leaves you spot a whole cozy nest full of lost and found treasures, all tidy and dry.

Robin lands on your shoulder and points with a wing. There is a bright red hat and a soft folded leaf, right next to each other.

You follow the bushy path where cool water trickles over smooth stones. Sam shows you how to step slow and gentle so no little bugs get a fright.

Robin finds a shady spot where two helpful things wait: a shiny puddle for a cool rinse, and a red hat snagged on a twig.

You carry the red hat back and plop it gently on the little monkey's head. The monkey squeals with joy and does three happy flips around the branch.

"Thank you, thank you," chatters the monkey. Sam beams, and Robin does a proud loop in the air. But you can still hear the elephant giggling by the river.

choices.text: Rest and share a snack first

pages.text:
You bring the soft leaf and the cool water to the ticklish elephant. Gently, you fan her trunk with the leaf and dab a little cool water on the tip.

The elephant takes a slow breath and, at last, no sneeze. "Oh, that feels lovely," she sighs happily. Sam cheers and Robin claps its wings.

choices.text: Go find the monkey's lost hat
Ask if any other animals need help

pages.text:
You reach the river where the elephant is still giggling and sneezing. You wave the soft leaf near her trunk, slow and steady, and hum a calm little tune.

Her trunk stops tickling, and she gives you the gentlest, happiest trunk-hug. Robin rides the hug like a fun ride.

You and Sam search until you spot the red hat snagged high on a vine. With a gentle boost and a careful reach, you set it free and bring it to the monkey.

The monkey hugs the hat, then hugs you. Robin sings a happy little jungle song that echoes through the trees.

choices.text: Look for one last friend to help

pages.text:
The monkey, the elephant, and a dozen giggly critters throw a parade in your honor. You lead the way with Sam while Robin tosses flower petals from above.

"The best explorers are the kindest ones," says Sam. You march home with a happy heart and a hat full of petals. The end.

Word spreads fast that two gentle helpers fixed every small problem in the jungle today. Animals line the trail to wave as you and Sam head for home.

Robin lands on your head and declares you an official Jungle Helper. You promise to come back tomorrow, because there is always a friend to help. The end.

You slip off to help a shy turtle who cannot flip back onto her feet. With a soft, careful tip, you set her right, and she blinks a grateful, sleepy smile.

No parade, no cheers, just a warm feeling that fills you up. Sam squeezes your hand and Robin nuzzles your cheek. Sometimes the quietest help is the biggest. The end.

You go looking for one last friend, and find a whole family of ducklings who each need a boost over a log. One by one, boop, boop, boop, you help them all across.

By the time you finish, the sun is setting in gold and pink. "Well," laughs Sam, "the jungle always has one more friend." You and Robin laugh too, and head home happy. The end.
